direction_notes: Stimulating forelimb or hindlimb motor cortex with the photoacoustic patch elicited time-locked EMG responses in the corresponding limb.
safety_notes: Bench test only: patch surface temperature rose from 30.9 C to 34.2 C after 1 h at 40 mJ/cm2, 10 Hz.

exposures.label: Photoacoustic patch over mouse forelimb and hindlimb motor cortex

target.label: forelimb motor cortex; hindlimb motor cortex

device.model: passive photoacoustic patch (spherical double logarithmic spiral CNT/PDMS array)

timing.protocol_description: Nanosecond laser pulses on CNT/PDMS emitters generate broadband optoacoustic transients; in vivo laser repetition, train length and number of stimulations not stated (bench tests used 8 ns pulses at 10 Hz, 1064 nm).

source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: Representative time- and frequency-domain analysis at the focus (Fig. 3C) showed a peak pressure up to 8 MPa, a dominant frequency component near 4.05 MHz, and broadband spectral content spanning 0–60 MHz.
source_quotes.exposures[0].unspecified_domain.pressure: Representative time- and frequency-domain analysis at the focus (Fig. 3C) showed a peak pressure up to 8 MPa, a dominant frequency component near 4.05 MHz, and broadband spectral content spanning 0–60 MHz.

flags.reason: Dominant component near 4.05 MHz from bench characterisation of a broadband (0-60 MHz) transient; in vivo frequency not separately stated.
